dedupe_keys.name: onslow water and sewer authority ransomware attack north carolina october 2018

description: This SiliconANGLE report of 16 October 2018 describes a ransomware attack on the Onslow Water and Sewer Authority in Jacksonville, North Carolina. Emotet infected the authority's network on 4 October 2018 and the Ryuk ransomware, which appeared in August 2018 and shares code with Hermes, was installed on 13 October, encrypting core computing systems. No customer data was reported stolen. The utility contacted the US Department of Homeland Security and the FBI, said it would not negotiate with criminals and did not pay, and faced a slow and costly rebuild. Coverage is one utility and one incident, in the weeks after Hurricane Florence. The article is free to read and states no licence. Caveats: it is a press account of the first days, so the final recovery cost and effect on treatment operations are not covered, and no technical data are given. For simulation, it is a documented cyber incident useful for resilience and emergency response scenarios of water utilities.
